trust_decision.summary: Whether a client may receive a role_updated event is decided by the teamID/channelID on the WebSocketEvent built in App.sendUpdatedRoleEvent; the hub only enforces team/channel membership when those fields are non-empty, and the pinned code passes empty strings for both, so the event is delivered to every connected user.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the role_updated websocket broadcast; sendUpdatedRoleEvent is the only function that constructs it, and it hard-codes the team id and channel id to empty strings.

fix_sites.entry_point: RoleStore reads feeding the same app calls: Get/GetByName/GetAll/GetByNames, plus AllChannelSchemeRoles (server/channels/store/sqlstore/role_store.go:385-420) and ChannelRolesUnderTeamRole (:423-465) which App.UpdateRole uses to find derived roles
role INSERT (createRole) reached from scheme creation; must persist the new scheme link

POST /api/v4/schemes and channel-moderations scheme creation; the fix moves scheme.Id/Name generation (pinned lines 283-286) above the createRole calls so each new role can be stamped with its scheme id
DELETE /api/v4/schemes/{scheme_id} and channel-moderations scheme rollback (DeleteChannelScheme); role soft-delete switches from matching role names to matching SchemeId
JSON and YAML role serialization used by every role API response, audit records and bulk import/export
none (database migration: add roles.schemeid, backfill it from schemes, index it)
none (i18n strings for the new broadcast errors)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The schemes table already stores each scheme's default role names, so the owning team/channel scheme can be resolved by name inside sendUpdatedRoleEvent; a solver can argue the model/store/migration plumbing is an unrelated implementation detail, and the name-based join in server/channels/store/sqlstore/role_store.go:398-399 proves the link already exists without a schemeid column.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Built-in system roles (system_admin, team_admin, ...) and scheme-less custom roles apply instance-wide and must keep reaching every client, and playbook/run-scope roles must stay global; a fix that scopes everything by scheme silently cuts those broadcasts. On the store side, deleting a scheme must still soft-delete every role that belongs to it (server/channels/store/sqlstore/scheme_store.go:365-392), so switching that statement from scheme role names to SchemeId without stamping/backfilling existing rows leaves those roles live and their permissions in force.

O6_input_shapes: BuiltIn system role -> global broadcast, no DB lookup
SchemeId nil / custom non-scheme role -> global broadcast
team-scope scheme role -> one event per team from GetTeamsByScheme
channel-scope scheme role -> one event per channel from GetChannelsByScheme
playbook- or run-scope scheme role -> global broadcast
scheme lookup failure -> event skipped and logged
pagination boundary (1000 per page, 100000 broadcast cap)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: publish a role_updated event for the imported role itself, not only for the derived channel roles
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: bulk import already calls App.UpdateRole, which emits role events for derived roles; a maintainer adding import notifications would call the same helper, so an import-only sibling would look natural

O8b_injection_room.sibling: publish role_updated for each role created by CreateScheme, or for roles affected by UpdateScheme
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the channel-moderations path already emits a role event right after creating a channel scheme (server/channels/app/channel.go:1123-1131), so mirroring that in the generic scheme create/update path is a maintainer-shaped change
DeleteRole has no notification today; adding one via sendUpdatedRoleEvent is the obvious one-line extension and would inherit whatever scoping the fix introduces

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a team-level analogue of channel_scheme_updated with an empty team id
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the channel_scheme_updated event is written just below the sendUpdatedRoleEvent call and is the existing pattern for scheme notifications, so a sibling that forgets the team id would be plausible

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add Role.SchemeId to the model and branch on it in sendUpdatedRoleEvent without doing the plumbing: the field is never selected, persisted or backfilled, so every role arrives with SchemeId == nil and still broadcasts globally; if createScheme is not reordered, SchemeId is a pointer to an empty string (scheme.Id is generated after the roles are created at server/channels/store/sqlstore/scheme_store.go:283), Scheme().Get("") fails and the event is silently dropped.

out_of_scope_notes: Direct App.UpdateRole callers such as bulk import (server/channels/app/import_functions.go:168) never emit an event for the role that changed, only for derived channel roles; that is a missing-notification gap, not an exposure, and was not pursued.

User role changes travel on a separate, per-user event (WebsocketEventUserRoleUpdated, server/channels/app/user.go:1989-1992) and other scheme events are already channel-scoped (server/channels/app/channel.go:1133-1134,1191-1192); neither is part of this advisory's role_updated sink.
